messages:
elyse_cs: Heads-up — ACME (account: acme-inc) just opened a P2 escalation. They say behaviour changed immediately after the weekly rollout (redwood-open-7b v2 -> v2.1) and a set of production prompts now returns much shorter, partial JSON and hallucinated fields. Internal evals all green, but customer-facing prompts fail. attaching sample below.

nate_eng-ml: thanks, can you paste the exact customer prompt + API request and the output they got? also which rollout/namespace?

elyse_cs: sure. rollout id: rollout/2024-11-08/v2.1 (canary -> full). customer prompt and observed output below. they're using hosted API from us-east-1. tokens/temp: temperature=0.0, max_tokens=600, top_p=0.95, stop=["\n\n"], stream=false

Customer prompt:
"""
You are a billing agent. Given the invoice text, extract a JSON object with keys: invoice_id, total_due, due_date, line_items (array with description and amount), and flagged (true if total_due > 5000). Return only JSON.
Invoice:
Invoice #11982
Date: 2024-10-12
Total: USD 12,450.00
Items:
 - Enterprise license: 12000.00
 - Discount: -1550.00
"""

Observed output (what ACME got):
"""
invoice_id: 11982
total: 12450
// then a paragraph of apology and unrelated marketing text, then truncated JSON start:
{
  "line_items": [
    {"descr": "Enterprise license", "amt": 12000}
  ]



(EOF)
"""

elyse_cs: they attached 8 more examples, all with similar pattern: earlier well-formed JSON, now either partial output, extra prose injection, wrong key names, or hallucinated negative charges. They say it started exactly at 2024-11-08T02:14:00Z which aligns with our full rollout timestamp.

deploy-bot: Deployment rollout/2024-11-08/v2.1 -> completed at 2024-11-08T02:12:47Z by deploy-ci. Canary (10%) started 2024-11-07T22:00Z.

monitor-bot: SLO alarms: small spike in token error rate at 2024-11-08T02:15Z. CPU/GPU metrics OK. Latency unchanged.

sam_support: @elyse_cs forwarded the customer's examples and a short recording. They've blocked an integration test because output is unexpected. If possible, give them a temporal rollback to v2 for that account. Can we pin them to previous model?

kevin_sre: we can route their account to the previous version by adding a route override. I can apply a temporary shard rule: route account_id: acme-inc -> redwood-open-7b@v2 (non-v2.1) for the next 72h. Want to wait for eng-ml investigation before switch?

nate_eng-ml: thanks for the data. Initial hypothesis: aggregator/regression introduced a distribution shift in tokenizer or postprocessing that interacts with strict JSON-only prompts at low temp. A few avenues: (1) check that model binary/quantization change in v2.1 didn't relax EOS/stop token handling, (2) check the instruction tuning dataset variant used for v2.1, (3) compare decoding logits for expected tokens in failing prompts.

jordi_eval: I looked at our eval harness — the internal JSON extraction suite (json-extract-suite) uses ~1200 prompts, mostly synthetic and shorter than customer prompts. Customer prompts are longer and include hyphenated invoice formats and currency tokens. So eval coverage gap is likely. Also our eval uses temperature=0.2 for some tests; they use 0.0 which can expose deterministic decoding issues.

priya_prod: to add context, v2.1 included two changes: a) retrained instruction-head with expanded safety/regression data, and b) switched default quantization path for some GPU types (int8 dynamic -> int8 static kernels). Both were flagged as low risk but bundled together.

nate_eng-ml: please run the following repro steps locally and paste the outputs here. Use the exact customer prompt and API parameters. Also collect logits for the first 30 tokens after prompt. Example commands:

```bash
# reproducible call via our test-cli (use api-key redacted)
redwood-cli generate --model redwood-open-7b@v2.1 \
  --temperature 0.0 --max-tokens 600 --stop "\\n\\n" \
  --prompt-file acme_sample1.txt --collect-logits > /tmp/acme_v21.json

redwood-cli generate --model redwood-open-7b@v2 \
  --temperature 0.0 --max-tokens 600 --stop "\\n\\n" \
  --prompt-file acme_sample1.txt --collect-logits > /tmp/acme_v2.json
```

nate_eng-ml: if v2 returns correct JSON and v2.1 doesn't, then it's a regression in the model artifact/decoding. If both fail, something else (runtime change) is suspicious.

elyse_cs: ran quick one in support console (not full logits) — v2 returned the clean JSON, v2.1 returned truncated + prose. gave results to @nate and attached raw output.

monitor-bot: telemetry snippet for that account: request_count=8, error_token_rate jumped from 0.2% -> 3.6% at 02:14Z. No auth failures.

nate_eng-ml: can we get the model metadata for v2.1 artifact hash and the training/tuning diffs? Also need the raw logits for the failing runs. @jordi_eval can you run the new eval harness with the customer's 9 prompts as a patch to see if v2.1 passes? We should also run with temperature=0.0 matching customer settings.

jordi_eval: running now — will add acme prompts as a temporary eval corpus (private), run at temp=0.0 and compare v2 vs v2.1. ETA ~2h.

priya_prod: agree with isolation: separate the two changes. If it is quantization kernel, we should be able to reproduce on dedicated dev-server with same hardware. @kevin_sre can you snapshot the GPU settings used for rollout and ensure we can replicate?

kevin_sre: GPU nodes for rollout: a100-80gb with int8-static kernel lib v1.3.2. grabbed container image digest and kernel logs from rollout time. uploading to /mnt/rollouts/2024-11-08/v2.1/infra_meta.tar.gz

nate_eng-ml: additional quick checks: compare tokenization boundaries for the invoice text between v2 and v2.1 tokenizers. If stop behavior changed, the model might not respect stop sequence and thus append prose. Also check that the stop sequence is forwarded to runtime unchanged (some routes strip arrays).

sam_support: customer requested ETA for fix and asked if we can rollback. They said integration tests are failing in staging. Please confirm whether routing override is safe.

kevin_sre: I can apply routing override now, but prefer to wait 30m for eng-ml to start tests. If we do override, we should record the change in incident log and set TTL to 72h.

nate_eng-ml: do the local repros first. If v2.1 fails reproducibly, we'll revert their account. If reproducible and tied to quant kernels, we can also produce a patch or revert kernel selection.

jordi_eval: quick update — initial run shows v2 passes all 9 ACME prompts at temp=0.0, v2.1 fails 7/9 with truncated JSON or extra prose. Attaching diffs (summary):
- Missing closing brace in 5/7 failures.
- Additional English sentences inserted before JSON in 4/7.
- Key renaming (invoice_id -> id) in 2/7.

jordi_eval: interestingly, some failures correlate with prompts that include both dollar signs and a dash line ("- Enterprise license"), maybe token boundary issue.

nate_eng-ml: that's enough to call it a regression. Next steps: (1) isolate whether quant kernel or instruction tuning affected decoding by running v2.1 weights on v2 runtime kernels and vice versa (weights swap), (2) collect logits and compute argmax token sequence to see where divergence begins, (3) revert customer routing if they want immediate fix.

priya_prod: setting priority to Sev-2 regression. I'll prepare a rollback plan: either (A) route affected accounts back to v2, or (B) patch v2.1 to use the old quantization path while we fix the instruction-tuning blend. Need eng-ml and infra check on compatibility.

kevin_sre: I will stage the route override in 15m unless eng-ml requests hold. Also will add a firewall so rollback is auditable.

elyse_cs: ACME prefers a soft rollback (route only their account) rather than global revert. They asked for a postmortem and communicated impact: integration tests failing in staging, but no live-data corruption. They appreciate quick response. :thumbsup:

nate_eng-ml: actionable owners: nate_eng-ml -> run kernel/weights swap and logits collection (ETA 4h), jordi_eval -> run expanded eval runs and produce PR for adding these prompts to regression suite (ETA 2h), kevin_sre -> prepare route override ready (ETA 15m), priya_prod -> coordinate rollback comms and incident page (ETA 1h).

deploy-bot: Canary metrics: 10% canary had 1.8% token errors, after 100% rollout peaked 3.6%.

monitor-bot: alert created: #inc-1248 JSON-extraction-regression; linked to thread 1742109452.

elyse_cs: I'll tell ACME we're preparing a per-account rollback and will follow up with timeline. Will post customer-facing note once we confirm routing change.

nate_eng-ml: quick debug note for later: compute KL divergence between distribution of next-token logits for v2 vs v2.1 on these prompts. If divergence spikes at a particular position, that's likely where tokenization/quantization changed argmax. Also check attention weights for instruction prompt tokens.

jordi_eval: finished runs: added ACME prompts to private suite and ran v2/v2.1 across the matrix (temperature 0.0, 0.2). Results attached to internal eval board. Opening PR to make these prompts permanent in regression checks.

kevin_sre: override applied for account acme-inc -> redwood-open-7b@v2, TTL 72h, change id: route-2024-11-08-acme-001. Audit log entry: /audit/routes/route-2024-11-08-acme-001.json

sam_support: informed ACME about per-account routing. They're testing and will confirm in ~30m. They asked for the eventual fix ETA — can we give an estimate now?

priya_prod: estimate depends on root cause: if quant kernel, likely 2-5 days for patch + validation; if instruction-tuning, could be multi-week depending on retrain/rollout cadence. We'll prioritize quant fix path first since low-risk.

nate_eng-ml: I'm starting weights/kernel swap now. Will post logs. If anyone has additional ACME prompts, drop them here.

elyse_cs: adding one extra failure case they sent (invoice with parentheses around amount). Also added their contact (ACME SRE: jane.doe@acme.com) to ticket.

monitor-bot: ACME test run (post-override) shows 100% success for their 9 sample prompts when routed to v2.

elyse_cs: ACME confirmed integration tests passed after routing override. Closing immediate customer impact. Keeping thread open for root cause and postmortem.

nate_eng-ml: update in 3h with logs. I'll also compute tokenization diffs and push any small mitigation (e.g., stronger stop enforcement) we can hotfix while full fix is prepared.

priya_prod: thanks team. I'll create incident page and postmortem template and assign follow-ups.

elyse_cs: thanks all. tagging this as follow-up: add ACME prompts to permanent eval, investigate quant kernel vs instruction-tune regress, determine whether we need additional canary checks for JSON-only prompts at temp=0.0.

(End of thread)
